ai_risk.summary: The biggest new item is a single Gizmodo report that Anthropic says an internal alarm for recursive self-improvement has been triggered. Details are not yet independently confirmed. At the UN autonomous-weapons talks in Geneva, Reuters reports that the US and Russia plan to oppose negotiations on limits, and the AI-agent exploit incident from yesterday now has a primary write-up. Central bankers at the Fed and ECB also named AI among the top risks to financial stability, but that warning is mainly about asset valuations and debt, so it is not listed as a separate item.

actions.summary: The clearest signals are still in active wars. Russia and Ukraine keep their manpower pipelines running around the talks, and the Houthis keep running mobilisation drives as the Yemen and Iran fronts heat up. Asian importers are moving toward shared oil stockpiles because of Hormuz disruption. European household-kit campaigns remain mostly scheduled, all-hazards programmes, and several viral 'stockpile now' claims were debunked this week. Confidence is moderate for the war-linked patterns and low for any reading of the household campaigns as preparation for a specific war.

patterns.points_to: Together the steps prepare for fighting around the Red Sea and Gulf to continue. The Houthis keep running village-by-village mobilisation drives. Israel is recalling reservists, and Egypt is building strategic reserves.
patterns.unsaid: Continued mobilisation alongside US statements that the Iran war is 'effectively over' (10 Nov) is consistent with regional governments planning for a longer conflict than Washington describes. The Houthi seizure of Mokha near Bab al-Mandeb points the same way.
patterns.plain_explanation: The Houthi mobilisation claims come only from Houthi-run media, which publishes such rallies routinely. Israel's recall is tied to a known manpower shortage. Egypt's reserves also guard against price shocks, not only war.
